75 and 84, with oldest-old age 85 and older (Lee et al., 2018). Although preventative care fostering a healthy 
cardiovascular system is the optimal desire, research indicates that there is an increase in cardiovascular disease as 
people age. The incidence of cardiovascular disease increases from approximately 40% in adults ages 40–59 to 
75% from ages 60–79, and approximately 86% in those above age 80 (Rodgers et al., 2019). Depending on the 
activity level of the client, the older adult typically needs about 2000 calories daily. Additionally, healthy older adults 
need increased dietary fiber, calcium, vitamin D, and potassium; healthy older adults should decrease their 
consumption of saturated fats, sodium, and added sugars (FDA, 2022a). See Table 12.7 for the recommended 
nutritional needs for later adulthood.
